blocks.title: Booking failure playbook
rows: Search request fails
Keep criteria, show retry and abort older requests
Results match the visible criteria
Offers expire while the tab is hidden
When the tab is visible again, rerun the search and mark changed prices
No hold starts from an expired offer
Hold response is lost
Retry createHold with the same key
One Reserve intent produces at most one hold
Class sells out
Show alternatives from the conflict response
Extras and driver details carry over
Price changes
Show old and new totals and ask for a new choice
Nobody confirms a price they have not seen
Hold expires
Move to hold-expired and Reserve again with a new key
Entered details remain intact
Reservation response is lost
Retry with the same key, then read the reservation
No duplicate reservation

blocks.text: Device clocks drift, so countdowns use expiresAt minus serverNow and re-base when a hidden tab becomes visible. The client timer is only a display: the server decides whether a hold is live, and confirming with an expired hold returns a conflict that the page handles like any other expiry.

blocks.title: Scenario walkthrough: the last compact SUV

steps.title: Two customers, one class
steps.text: Two customers view the same airport branch and see a compact SUV offer from the same availability snapshot.

steps.title: First Reserve wins
steps.text: The first createHold succeeds. The second returns sold-out with a midsize alternative at a server price.

steps.title: Details survive
steps.text: The second page keeps the child seat and driver details, announces the change, and moves focus to the alternatives list.

steps.title: No phantom booking
steps.text: If the first hold expires, the class returns to the server pool, and the second customer sees it only after a fresh search.

blocks.alt: Vehicle hold lifecycle from offer to active hold, warning and extension, expiry, a new Reserve with a fresh key, and the held, price-changed or sold-out outcomes.
blocks.caption: Hold lifecycle: the server clock decides expiry, and every outcome keeps the customer's details.
blocks.fallbackText: Text fallback: An offer becomes an active hold. A warning can extend it. An expired hold needs a new Reserve with a new key, which returns held, price-changed with both totals, or sold-out with alternatives.

blocks.title: Booking tests that protect customers
items: Double-click Reserve; assert one idempotency key and one hold.
Lose the hold response; assert the retry reaches the same hold.
Expire a hold during driver details; assert input survives and Reserve uses a new key.
Return price-changed; assert both totals appear before any confirmation.
Search from a device in another zone; assert branch-local times in the URL, the UI and the request.
Run keyboard and screen-reader passes over date entry, the results count, the hold warning and alternatives.

blocks.text: Measure hold expiry, price-changed and sold-out conflicts, search-to-hold and hold-to-reservation conversion, segmented by branch, device class and network. Tune caching and warning timing from those numbers rather than from fixed guesses.
